exams.title: From sea to supply
exams.challenge: An eight-stage technical sequence requires accurate process language and careful separation of treatment from distribution.

task1.title: Producing drinking water by reverse osmosis
task1.prompt: The diagram below shows the stages used to turn seawater into drinking water by reverse osmosis.

figure.title: Seawater treatment by reverse osmosis
figure.aria: Process diagram showing eight stages in producing drinking water from seawater by reverse osmosis.

steps.title: Seawater intake
steps.detail: Seawater is drawn from offshore through an intake pipe fitted with a coarse screen.

steps.title: Initial screening
steps.detail: The screen removes larger debris before the water enters the treatment plant.

steps.title: Pre-treatment
steps.detail: Fine filters and conditioning chemicals reduce suspended particles that could damage the membranes.

steps.title: Pressurisation
steps.detail: Pumps raise the pressure of the filtered seawater to the level required by the membranes.

steps.title: Membrane separation
steps.detail: Reverse-osmosis membranes allow water molecules through while retaining most dissolved salts.

steps.title: Mineral adjustment
steps.detail: The low-mineral permeate is remineralised and its pH is adjusted to make it suitable for supply.

steps.title: Disinfection
steps.detail: A final disinfection stage controls microorganisms before storage.

steps.title: Storage and distribution
steps.detail: Treated water is stored in a covered reservoir and then pumped into the municipal network.

figure.caption: Stages shown in order; details are simplified for writing practice.
